items.headline: Update: Singapore haze holds in the moderate range for a second day as Sumatra fires drift smoke
items.summary: The central region logged a 24-hour PSI of 92 on Sept 7, a second day of improved readings, but the NEA warned that persistent dry conditions and smoke plumes from fires in southern Sumatra and West Kalimantan could push air quality back into the unhealthy band.

items.headline: MAS survey lifts Singapore's 2026 growth forecast to 5% on an AI-driven tech upturn
items.summary: Private economists in the Monetary Authority of Singapore's latest quarterly survey raised their 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5%, up from 3.5% in June, citing a sustained AI-led technology cycle; the economy grew 5.9% year-on-year in the second quarter.

items.headline: Update: Probe widens into 52 Singaporeans detained in China over a suspected pyramid scheme
items.summary: More victims and organisers have surfaced in the case of 52 Singaporeans detained in Guangxi over a suspected pyramid scheme, with fresh reports of a local celebrity allegedly present at recruitment meetings and investors who flew to China after being invited to 'do business'.

items.headline: Delhi High Court orders an audit of all PGs and hostels after the Satya Niketan building collapse
items.summary: The Delhi High Court directed a citywide audit of paying-guest accommodations and hostels following the fatal Satya Niketan building collapse; police arrested the wife and son of the property owner as the safety of student housing near south Delhi colleges came under scrutiny.

items.headline: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Sanjay Agrawal as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Sanjay Agrawal to be Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, amid a row over the acting chief justice that saw a top-court judge write to the Chief Justice of India seeking a transfer, reviving debate on judicial accountability.

items.headline: Election Commission announces bypolls for six seats, including in West Bengal
items.summary: The Election Commission announced by-elections for six assembly seats, among them constituencies in West Bengal, sharpening questions over whether Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee will again contest Nandigram ahead of next year's state polls.

items.headline: IMD warns of extremely heavy rain in Chhattisgarh as a monsoon surge lashes central India
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department warned of extremely heavy rainfall in Chhattisgarh and very heavy rain across eastern Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and the Northeast, with authorities on alert in Varanasi and Chitrakoot as rivers swelled.

items.headline: India sends a tunnel-rescue team and 57 tonnes of relief to flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: India deployed an 11-member tunnel-rescue reconnaissance team and airlifted more than 57 tonnes of relief supplies to Nepal, where floods and landslides along the border have killed over 1,000 people and left thousands missing.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The allowed UK outlets (BBC and Sky News) were unreachable to the routine's research tool, and the fallback tier (The Guardian, CNN, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, CNBC) surfaced no verifiable UK-domestic story from the last 48 hours; a placeholder is shown rather than an unverified or off-window item.

items.headline: AfD wins Germany's Saxony-Anhalt election with a record 44%, but falls short of a majority
items.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany took about 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, its strongest-ever state result, winning 39 of 83 seats — three short of a majority. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU slumped to 17.2%, and co-leader Alice Weidel predicted federal elections 'before Christmas'.

items.headline: Death toll from the Nepal-China floods passes 1,000 with more than 4,400 missing
items.summary: Catastrophic flooding and landslides across Nepal and China's Xizang region have killed more than 1,000 people, with over 4,400 still missing, as rescue crews from Nepal, China and India work to reach communities cut off by mudslides.

items.headline: Update: Ukraine peace push stalls as Zelensky says 'we expect the war will continue'
items.summary: After Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner shuttled between Moscow and Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects the war to continue and is counting on US energy and air-defence support this winter; a three-day pause on strikes against the two capitals lapsed as Russian attacks resumed.

items.headline: Update: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte posts bail in the Marcos threat case
items.summary: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte posted bail after a court issued an arrest warrant over allegations she publicly threatened to have President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and two others assassinated, deepening the rupture between the country's two most powerful political families.

items.headline: Update: OpenAI launches GPT-6 'Astra' and declares the arrival of the AGI era
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, which president Greg Brockman called a generational leap and, potentially, the arrival of artificial general intelligence; the model rolled out first to enterprise and cybersecurity customers, with ChatGPT and API access phasing in over the following days at $10 per million input and $50 per million output tokens.

items.headline: Microsoft releases MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech model it says beats OpenAI, Google and ElevenLabs
items.summary: Microsoft AI unveiled MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech-recognition model it says is faster, more accurate and cheaper than rival services, with introductory pricing of $0.10 per audio hour through the end of 2026.

items.headline: Attackers exploit a critical Langflow flaw to run code and steal API keys
items.summary: Security researchers say attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Langflow, an open-source framework for building AI apps, that lets unauthenticated users run Python remotely; observed attacks tried to extract secrets including OpenAI API keys and AWS credentials.

items.headline: China's Moonshot AI files confidentially for a Hong Kong IPO, seeking up to US$5 billion
items.summary: Moonshot AI, the Beijing maker of the Kimi models, filed confidentially for a Hong Kong listing and is said to be seeking as much as US$5 billion, having been valued around US$50 billion in an ongoing funding round, with Bank of America, CICC, Deutsche Bank and Goldman Sachs on the deal.

items.headline: Asian shares rally as Japan's Nikkei jumps 2% and South Korea's Kospi opens up 3%
items.summary: Asian markets advanced on Sept 7 as AI-linked technology stocks led gains: Japan's Nikkei 225 rose about 2% above 66,300 and the broader Topix added 0.8%, while South Korea's Kospi opened up 3.1%; Hong Kong's Hang Seng was little changed. US markets were shut for Labor Day.

items.headline: Crusoe and Fluidstack lead the week's biggest venture rounds in an AI-infrastructure haul
items.summary: Data-centre and cloud provider Crusoe raised about US$3 billion and Fluidstack US$1.5 billion, topping the week's venture financings as capital kept pouring into the power-hungry infrastructure behind the AI boom.

items.headline: Markets split near 50/50 on a September Fed hike as August CPI looms
items.summary: Traders are near evenly divided on whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates 25 basis points at its Sept 15-16 meeting, after hawkish signals from Chair Kevin Warsh and a hot August jobs report; the August CPI due Sept 11 is seen as the pivotal input.

items.headline: Nvidia's investment footprint swells to about US$99 billion as it expands its reach
items.summary: Nvidia's web of investments across AI startups and infrastructure has grown to roughly US$99 billion, underscoring how the chipmaker is using its balance sheet to entrench its position across the AI supply chain.

items.headline: 🎾 Tiafoe edges Medvedev in a two-tie-break battle to reach the US Open quarter-finals
items.summary: Frances Tiafoe beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(1), 6-4, 7-6(6) in straight sets to book a US Open quarter-final, where he will face Alex Michelsen in an all-American last-eight tie.

items.headline: 🎾 Shelton dismisses Tsitsipas to set up a US Open quarter-final with Alcaraz
items.summary: Ben Shelton beat Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 to reach the US Open quarter-finals, where he meets defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, who dropped just three sets on his way through the fourth round.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli stretches his F1 title lead to 66 points after Monza, with the Madrid GP next
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli's win from 19th on the grid at Monza pushed his championship lead over Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 66 points, with Lewis Hamilton a further 10 back in third; the season now heads to the new Madrid circuit for the Spanish Grand Prix on Sept 11-13.

items.headline: 🏏 India and Sri Lanka reach the Women's Asia Cup semi-finals in Dubai
items.summary: India and defending champions Sri Lanka both sealed top-two group finishes to reach the Women's Asia Cup semi-finals, which will be played on Sept 10 and 11 at the Dubai International Stadium.

items.headline: Detailed maps of breast tumours reveal hidden pockets of dormant cancer cells
items.summary: Researchers mapping breast tumours in fine spatial detail uncovered reservoirs of dormant cancer cells that can lie quiet for years, a finding that may help explain why breast cancer sometimes returns long after treatment.

items.headline: Princeton's AI controller steers fusion plasma in milliseconds, faster than humans
items.summary: Princeton researchers tested an AI system that monitors and adjusts fusion plasma within milliseconds, reacting far faster than a human operator to suppress the instabilities that can quench a reaction — a step toward keeping future fusion reactors stable.

items.headline: Indonesia's peat fires surge early as El Nino and drought dry out wetlands
items.summary: Indonesia's dangerous peat fires are flaring unusually early in the 2026 season as a strengthening El Nino and severe drought dry out wetlands that can smoulder underground for months — the same fires now drifting haze toward Singapore and Malaysia.

items.headline: Astronomers spot young 'switched-off' radio galaxies whose black-hole jets have died
items.summary: Astronomers identified a surprisingly young population of fading radio galaxies whose supermassive black holes have already switched off their powerful jets, offering a rare look at how these cosmic engines flicker out.

fun_fact.headline: Mauna Kea is taller than Everest measured from base to peak
fun_fact.body: Measured from its base rather than from sea level, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is the tallest mountain on Earth — taller even than Mount Everest. Its summit stands 4,207 m above sea level, but the volcano's base lies about 6,000 m down on the Pacific floor, giving a total height of roughly 10,210 m, well above Everest's 8,849 m. Everest still holds the record for the highest point above sea level; Mauna Kea wins base-to-peak.

puzzle.title: Paper Trail
puzzle.body:
Take a square sheet of paper.
Fold it exactly in half with a horizontal fold, then fold it in half again with a vertical fold. You now hold a small square that is four layers thick.
With a hole punch, punch ONE hole through all four layers, placing it near the folded corner (the corner where both folds meet).
Now unfold the paper completely.
How many holes are in the sheet, and how are they arranged?
puzzle.approach: Track how each fold doubles the number of layers, then mirror the single punch back across every fold line.
puzzle.answer:
Four holes.
Two folds stack the paper into 2 x 2 = 4 layers, so one punch pierces four layers and unfolds into four holes.
The folded corner where both creases meet is the CENTRE of the original sheet, so the four holes sit symmetrically around the middle of the page — one in each quadrant, each the mirror image of the others across the horizontal and vertical fold lines — forming a small square cluster near the centre.

word_puzzle.title: Rope's End
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange all eleven letters of the phrase

   A ROPE ENDS IT

into a single eleven-letter word that names exactly the feeling that phrase evokes.
Every letter is used once, and no letter is left over.
word_puzzle.approach: The phrase is a cryptic definition of its own answer — count the letters (11) and think of the feeling it describes.
word_puzzle.answer:
DESPERATION.
The letters of A ROPE ENDS IT — A, R, O, P, E, E, N, D, S, I, T — are exactly the letters A, D, E, E, I, N, O, P, R, S, T of DESPERATION.
Fittingly, 'a rope ends it' is a cryptic description of the answer.
